mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS decline over 3 months falls below 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS declines.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate remains above 5.0% for 3 months but S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicate a broad-based economic slowdown in consumer demand and business activity, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and INDPRO fails to predict negative returns, with the Rank IC falling below 0.03 or the negative return rate being less than 55% in triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% and rising, the increased cost of borrowing depresses corporate investment and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months reflects strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS growth over 3 months falls below 0.03 in any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS grows.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in the residential construction sector that reduces economic activity and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Housing starts remain below 1200 for two months but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) create a stagflationary environment that erodes corporate margins and consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and UNRATE > 5.0% fails to predict negative returns, with the Rank IC below 0.03 or the negative return rate less than 55% in triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-growth economic regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a supply shock that disrupts manufacturing and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In high-growth economic periods, a decline in INDPRO does not lead to negative S&P 500 returns, with positive returns occurring in more than 55% of cases or Rank IC below 0.03.
